[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Object Detection in Computer Vision: R-CNN, YOLO, and SSD"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Object detection is a core computer vision task that involves identifying instances of objects in images or videos and localizing them with bounding boxes. Unlike image classification, which only assigns a single label to an entire image, object detection requires predicting both the class and the spatial coordinates for multiple objects simultaneously."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Evolution of Object Detection Architectures"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Modern object detection models are broadly categorized into two main paradigms: Two-stage detectors and One-stage detectors. Two-stage detectors separate region proposal from classification and bounding box regression, achieving high accuracy. One-stage detectors frame detection as a single regression problem, prioritizing inference speed."},{"order":5,"type":"subheading","text":"1. The R-CNN Family (Two-Stage Detectors)"},{"order":6,"type":"paragraph","text":"The R-CNN (Regions with CNN features) family revolutionized object detection by applying deep convolutional networks to region proposals."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"R-CNN: Uses an external algorithm like Selective Search to extract roughly 2,000 region proposals per image. Each proposal is warped and fed independently through a CNN, followed by Support Vector Machines (SVMs) for classification."},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Fast R-CNN: Passes the entire image through the CNN once to generate a feature map. Region proposals are then projected onto this feature map and extracted using RoI (Region of Interest) pooling, drastically reducing computational redundancy."},{"order":9,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Faster R-CNN: Replaced the slow selective search algorithm with a fully differentiable Region Proposal Network (RPN), making the entire pipeline end-to-end trainable and achieving near real-time performance."},{"order":10,"type":"subheading","text":"2. YOLO - You Only Look Once (One-Stage Detector)"},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"Introduced by Joseph Redmon et al., YOLO frames object detection as a single regression problem, straight from image pixels to bounding box coordinates and class probabilities."},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"The input image is divided into an S x S grid."},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"If an object's center falls into a grid cell, that grid cell is responsible for predicting it."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Each cell predicts B bounding boxes, confidence scores for those boxes, and C conditional class probabilities."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Because predictions are computed in a single forward pass through the network, YOLO models are exceptionally fast and suitable for real-time video processing."},{"order":16,"type":"subheading","text":"3. SSD - Single Shot MultiBox Detector"},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"SSD strikes a balance between the speed of YOLO and the accuracy of two-stage detectors by utilizing multi-scale feature maps."},{"order":18,"type":"bullet_point","text":"It uses a base network for feature extraction followed by auxiliary convolutional layers that progressively decrease in size."},{"order":19,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Predictions (bounding boxes and class scores) are made at multiple feature map scales, allowing the model to naturally handle objects of various sizes (small objects in deep layers, large objects in shallow layers)."},{"order":20,"type":"subheading","text":"Implementation Example: Torchvision Faster R-CNN"},{"order":21,"type":"paragraph","text":"Below is a Python code snippet utilizing PyTorch and Torchvision to load a pre-trained Faster R-CNN model and perform inference on an image."},{"order":22,"type":"code","text":"import torch
from torchvision.models.detection import fasterrcnn_resnet50_fpn, FasterRCNN_ResNet50_FPN_Weights
from torchvision.transforms import functional as F
from PIL import Image

# Load pre-trained weights
weights = FasterRCNN_ResNet50_FPN_Weights.DEFAULT
model = fasterrcnn_resnet50_fpn(weights=weights)
model.eval()

# Load and preprocess an image
image = Image.open("test_image.jpg").convert("RGB")
image_tensor = F.to_tensor(image).unsqueeze(0)

# Perform inference
with torch.no_grad():
    predictions = model(image_tensor)

# Print detected boxes and labels
print("Bounding Boxes:", predictions[0]['boxes'])
print("Labels:", predictions[0]['labels'])
print("Scores:", predictions[0]['scores'])"},{"order":23,"type":"subheading","text":"Comparison Summary"},{"order":24,"type":"bullet_point","text":"R-CNN Family: High accuracy, traditionally slower inference, excellent for fine-grained localization."},{"order":25,"type":"bullet_point","text":"YOLO: Extremely fast, great for real-time applications, highly optimized for edge devices and video feeds."},{"order":26,"type":"bullet_point","text":"SSD: Fast single-shot inference with improved handling of multi-scale objects compared to early YOLO variants."}]
